candidates.filename: StateLibQld 2 67803 Kit inspections at the new female division of the Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.jpg
candidates.caption:
Kit inspections at the new female division of the Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.
Female prisoners are standing in a line having their kits inspected at the new women's prison. A full prisoner's kit consisted of a chemise; a blue and white striped petticoat; a gown; a pair of coarse white stockings (all branded); a red cotton pocket handkerchief; a white apron; and a white mob cap with frills and strings to be tied under the chin. Other items were a pair of strong lace-up boots; a comb; a spoon; and a navy blue and white kerchief for the neck (Information taken from: The Queenslander, 28 November, 1903, p. 21).
candidates.sourceFamily: commons:statelibqld 2 67803 kit inspections at the new female division of the boggo road gaol, brisbane, 1903.jpg

candidates.filename: StateLibQld 2 70991 Prisoners having dinner in the exercise yard at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.jpg
candidates.caption:
Prisoners having dinner in the exercise yard at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.
Female prisoners are sitting down to a meal at the new women's prison in Brisbane. The inmates are dressed in their uniforms, including bonnets and aprons. 'Tin plates were being filled with the allotted portions of meat and potatoes, and tin pannikins with soup. These were then placed in huge wooden four-handled trays, each carried by two women to the exercise yards, where some of the prisoners dined at tables in the shelter sheds' (Information taken from: The Queenslander, 28 November, 1903, p. 21).
candidates.sourceFamily: commons:statelibqld 2 70991 prisoners having dinner in the exercise yard at the new female division of boggo road gaol, brisbane, 1903.jpg

candidates.caption:
Warders' quarters at Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.
Exterior view of the warders' quarters at Boggo Road Gaol. A warder is standing in front of a white picket fence that encloses a small yard outside the quarters. A child is riding a tricycle outside the fence gate. 'The buildings, which comprise the five separate blocks, are surrounded by a massive brick wall, 20ft. in height, the only opening in which is the main entrance, a massive pair of iron gates, which admit the visitor to a lofty vestibule which has on one side a guard-room and entrance lodge and warders' quarters.' (Information taken from: The Queenslander, 28 November, 1903, p. 22).

candidates.filename: StateLibQld 2 68047 Dinner preparations at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.jpg
candidates.caption:
Dinner preparations at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.
Interior view of three women preparing meals in the kitchen at the new female division of the Brisbane Prison. The kitchen is 'most admirably appointed. It is fitted with three large coppers, set in brick and cement, water being supplied to each from a separate tap. The range is a fine double-oven range by Lupton, and is fitted with a patent double coil hot water apparatus, which supplies hot water to all parts of the building. Two large double-handled refuse bins are provided, and substantial wooden tables' (Information taken from: The Queenslander, 28 November, 1903).
candidates.sourceFamily: commons:statelibqld 2 68047 dinner preparations at the new female division of boggo road gaol, brisbane, 1903.jpg

candidates.filename: StateLibQld 2 75473 Prisoners using the laundry facilities at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.jpg
candidates.caption:
Prisoners using the laundry facilities at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.
Interior view of prisoners working in the laundry at the new women's prison. The inmates are washing in tubs lining the wall as others sort through linen in a separate area in the background. Laundry baskets can be seen on the floor to the left. A superviser, standing in the middle of the photograph, is overseeing the work. 'In the laundry a big wash was in progress, and, judging by the whiteness of the linen seen in the ironing room there must be some good laundresses amongst the inmates...

The laundry is a beautifully cool and well ventilated room, containing eight fixed tubs, to which both pipe water and soft water are supplied by taps. There are four large washing coppers set in brickwork and cement, and these are provided with canopy-shaped ventilators. There are seven large windows, and two double doors. The latter are of iron, and the windows, like all the others in the establishment, are secured with massive iron bars' (Information taken from: The Queenslander, 28 November, 1903, pp. 21, 22).
candidates.sourceFamily: commons:statelibqld 2 75473 prisoners using the laundry facilities at the new female division of boggo road gaol, brisbane, 1903.jpg

candidates.filename: StateLibQld 2 72267 Matron's quarters at Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.jpg
candidates.caption:
Matron's quarters at Boggo Road Gaol, Brisbane, 1903.
Exterior view of the matron's quarters at the new female division of Boggo Road Gaol. A woman is standing on the lower verandah. 'The buildings, which comprise the five separate blocks, are surrounded by a massive brick wall, 20ft. in height, the only opening in which is the main entrance, a pair of iron gates, which admit the visitor to a lofty vestibule which has on one side a guard-room and entrance lodge and warder's quarters, and on the other the matron's quarters. The latter have no communication with the interior of the gaol, but are approached from the outside by a separate entrance.' (Information taken from: The Queenslander, 28 November, 1903, p. 21).
